{{Short description|Concept in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Zariski geometry''' consists of an abstract structure introduced by [[Ehud Hrushovski]] and [[Boris Zilber]], in order to give a characterisation of the [[Zariski topology]] on an [[algebraic curve]], and all its powers. The Zariski topology on a product of [[algebraic varieties]] is very rarely the [[product topology]], but richer in closed sets defined by equations that mix two sets of variables. The result described gives that a very definite meaning, applying to [[projective curve]]s and [[compact Riemann surface]]s in particular.

== Definition ==

A '''Zariski geometry''' consists of a set ''X'' and a [[topological structure]] on each of the sets

:''X'', ''X''<sup>2</sup>, ''X''<sup>3</sup>, ...

satisfying certain axioms.

(N) Each of the ''X''<sup>''n''</sup> is a [[Noetherian topological space]], of dimension at most ''n''.

Some standard terminology for Noetherian spaces will now be assumed.

(A) In each ''X''<sup>''n''</sup>, the subsets defined by equality in an ''n''-[[tuple]] are closed. The mappings
: ''X''<sup>''m''</sup> → ''X''<sup>''n''</sup>
defined by projecting out certain coordinates and setting others as constants are all continuous.

(B) For a  projection

: ''p'': ''X''<sup>''m''</sup> → ''X''<sup>''n''</sup>

and an [[irreducible set|irreducible]] closed subset ''Y'' of ''X''<sup>''m''</sup>, ''p''(''Y'') lies between its closure ''Z'' and ''Z'' \ ''{{prime|Z}}'' where ''{{prime|Z}}'' is a proper closed subset of ''Z''. (This is [[quantifier elimination]], at an abstract level.)

(C) ''X'' is irreducible.

(D) There is a uniform bound on the number of elements of a fiber in a projection of any closed set in ''X''<sup>''m''</sup>, other than the cases where the fiber is ''X''.

(E) A closed irreducible subset of ''X''<sup>''m''</sup>, of dimension ''r'', when intersected with a diagonal subset in which ''s'' coordinates are set equal, has all components of dimension at least ''r'' &minus; ''s'' + 1.

The further condition required is called ''very ample'' (cf. [[very ample line bundle]]).  It is assumed there is an irreducible closed subset ''P'' of some ''X''<sup>''m''</sup>, and an irreducible closed subset ''Q'' of ''P''× ''X''<sup>2</sup>, with the following properties:

(I) Given pairs (''x'', ''y''), (''{{prime|x}}'', ''{{prime|y}}'') in  ''X''<sup>2</sup>, for some ''t'' in ''P'', the set of (''t'', ''u'', ''v'') in ''Q'' includes (''t'', ''x'', ''y'') but not (''t'', ''{{prime|x}}'', ''{{prime|y}}'')

(J) For ''t'' outside a proper closed subset of ''P'', the set of (''x'', ''y'') in ''X''<sup>2</sup>,  (''t'', ''x'', ''y'') in ''Q'' is an irreducible closed set of dimension 1.

(K) For all pairs  (''x'', ''y''), (''{{prime|x}}'', ''{{prime|y}}'') in  ''X''<sup>2</sup>, selected from outside a proper closed subset, there is some ''t'' in ''P'' such that the set of (''t'', ''u'', ''v'') in ''Q'' includes (''t'', ''x'', ''y'') and (''t'', ''{{prime|x}}'', ''{{prime|y}}'').

Geometrically this says there are enough curves to separate points (I), and to connect points (K); and that such curves can be taken from a single [[parametric family]].

Then Hrushovski and Zilber prove that under these conditions there is an [[algebraically closed field]] ''K'', and a [[Algebraic curve#Singularities|non-singular]] [[algebraic curve]] ''C'', such that its Zariski geometry of powers and their [[Zariski topology]] is isomorphic to the given one. In short, the geometry can be algebraized.
